# Out-of-Profile Deal

`sales.sit.out_of_profile_deal` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

Owned by `sales.market_and_targeting.icp_definition`


> A live deal decaying in the way accounts outside the profile characteristically decay: interest without economics, engagement without a funded buyer, effort scaling faster than the contract value. What distinguishes it from the stalled-deal situations its neighbours own is the question asked, not the symptoms observed — deal review and pipeline management ask how to un-stall it, and this asks whether it should have been in pipeline at all. Both readings are legitimate on the same deal and they lead opposite ways, which is why this situation deliberately loads none of the relationship objects a rescue plan would need. The second purpose is calibration: a deal ending is the only moment the profile receives evidence, and a stall closed out without a fit reading is a lesson thrown away.


## Layer 2 binding

The join that makes this situation reachable. An unbound situation never compiles, and nothing errors when it doesn't.

- `stalled_deal`
- `cooling_deal`
- `closed_lost_risk`


Narrowed by `deal.status = open`

## Metadata

owner **Sales** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Bound to three deal-decay types, all shared with capabilities that will read them differently — that overlap is intended, because a stalling deal genuinely has two honest readings and the expensive error is running only the rescue one. Unlike the inbound situation, most of the knowledge loaded here can actually fire today: the executable patterns on Fit Analysis and Disqualifier all key off deal behaviour, which is exactly what Layer 2 emits. The gap that would improve this situation most is a loss REASON on closed_lost_mention — without it every reading taken here dies with the deal instead of grouping into the loss cohort that would evidence a disqualifier.
